touches.text: Owns the inspectors and gates (draft, moving from standalone): build_inspector, plan_inspector, ticket_inspector, corrosion, exemptions, rehearsal, determinism, import_sieve, and the tester (11; Q#33, Akien 2026-10-29). (Not diagnostic_inspector: it is base's, 17.3.) The code pipeline's inspectors and gates move to CodeMother; any that are not about code (if such existed) would not. (Q#31, Akien 2026-10-27)
Every call makes an inference ticket (3.3.2): trees first, then the cheapest route the nest finds.
Machine: route — the sieves (enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed), built with the nest tool, cheapest survivor first.
build_inspector: python sieves run after a build; reds a component that fails one (no charter, no proofs, a silent device, ...). "We find a new thing, we add a new sieve." → CodeMother (10.3.5)
import_sieve: one parse of every .py into an import graph; what reaches what. Enforces "only the proxy reaches the host/database" and RULE 1. → CodeMother

conflicts.text: Bands are phases: preprocess, measure, postprocess.
conflicts.ticket_says: Band 1 is 'record' (and bands are preprocess/record/postprocess, measured from BAND_NAMES = {0: preprocess, 1: record, 2: postprocess})
conflicts.why: Outline states 'Bands are phases: preprocess, measure, postprocess' but the ticket's measured evidence (from cairn/tools/base/nest.py:28) shows the code currently uses 'record' for band 1, not 'measure'. The outline's band terminology contradicts what the actual codebase declares. Both cannot stand because band 1 cannot be simultaneously named 'measure' (outline) and 'record' (code/ticket).
